json.answer:
The P.I. has completed human subjects training. The research assistants will be required to
complete human subjects training through the UCR Office of Research and Economic
Development.
The project will be submitted to the campus Institutional Review Board and requested revisions
to the project based on feedback from the IRB will be incorporated prior to data collection.

question.text: The researchers will ask all respondents to sign informed consent forms prior to interviews, as

json.answer:
well as in connection with the collection of survey data. These consent forms will include
information about how confidentiality of responses will be protected.

question.text: The longevity analysis will collect data on the length of time clusters have operated (including

json.answer:
the length of time between first hires and closures for those that have disbanded). We will
collect data from a minimum of 36 institutions, attempting to find dates of operation for all
clusters authorized at those institutions. The total number of clusters cannot be estimated at this
time but is likely to encompass as many as 150-200.

question.text: The comparative analysis will collect data on performance and attitudes from cluster

json.answer:
participants. The performance data will include publications, citations, research grants, patents,
licenses, and start-ups founded by members of interdisciplinary cluster hires, as well as those of
a matched sample of faculty hired through normal departmental mechanisms. The survey data
will include responses to five-page surveys from members of the interdisciplinary clusters. The
P.I. will also collect interview data from cluster leads and university administrators.

question.text: Performance and survey responses will be collected from a minimum of 72 individuals affiliated

json.answer:
with interdisciplinary clusters (at least three individuals from four institutions each in six fields),
and a matched sample of at least 72 individuals hired through normal departmental channels.

question.text: Interview data will be collected from a minimum of 24 cluster leads and four administrators. If

json.answer:
fields are drawn from multiple institutions, the number of interviews with cluster leads will
reflect the number of institutions and the number of fields included in the sample. The number
of interviews with university administrators will reflect the number of institutions included in the
sample.

question.text: The members of the project team will spot check coding on a 10 percent sample of individuals

json.answer:
hired through cluster programs and a 10 percent sample of individual hired through normal
departmental procedures. If problems arise in the validation of coding, more extensive checks

question.text: will be conducted. Coders will be instructed on the requirements for producing high quality

json.answer:
data, including meticulousness, conscientiousness, asking questions where uncertainties exist,
and double checking work.

question.text: Data will be backed up on a weekly basis on a hard drive kept in a locked cabinet in the project

json.answer:
office. The data will be preserved exclusively on the two project computers and the back-up
hard drive.

question.text: Performance and survey data will be coded into STATA data files, including numeric

json.answer:
institutional and cluster identifiers, for subsequent data analysis. Data collected from individual
and institutions will be stripped of institutional identifications and given a letter title
corresponding to the institution’s name. The University of California, Riverside, for example,

question.text: might be labelled “Institution A.” Interviews will be tape recorded for consultation during the

json.answer: writing of papers and reports. To our knowledge, there will be little overlap between the data

question.text: collected for this project and data collected by other researchers. The only project that may

json.answer:
include overlapping data is that of Erin Leahey at the University of Arizona (SciSIP award
#1461989). However, consultation with Prof. Leahey has led us to conclude that the amount of
overlap is quite limited to the extent that it exists at all.

question.text: Prof. Leahey’s work is focused on support for interdisciplinary activities on university campuses

json.answer:
and includes evidence on university investments in interdisciplinary activities. In previous work,
Prof. Leahey has collected data on publication rates and publication prominence of scholars

question.text: working in interdisciplinary teams relative to scholars who are not working in such teams. We

json.answer: see little overlap in these data and the data the research team intends to collect. A robust study of

question.text: interdisciplinary activity has been conducted at Stanford University by Prof. Daniel MacFarland.

json.answer:
Although these data are relevant to our work, they are not exclusively or primarily focused on
cluster hires. We do not intend to integrate either of these databases with the data we collect.

question.text: All data will be coded and saved on password-protected computers in the project office. No data

json.answer:
will be removed from the project office during the period of the project. The only individuals
with access to the collected data will be the P.I. and research assistants. New research assistants

question.text: will be advised of the essential care that must be taken with data collected for this project. Any

json.answer:
research assistants found to be handling data in a careless way will be immediately removed
from the project staff.

question.text: No names of individuals or institutions will be used in papers prepared by the project team

json.answer: without the explicit consent of the individuals and institutions.

question.text: Data from the project will be preserved in data files stripped of individual and institutional

json.answer:
names. These data files will include a small number of variables that will allow researchers to
categorize the institutions. These variables include institutional size, Carnegie category, control

question.text: (private, non-profit or public), and regional location. Following the completion of the project,

json.answer: the data archive will be made available on the project website to researchers who are interested

question.text: in pursuing questions related to cluster hiring. The preservation format will be platform-

json.answer: independent. Following the end of the project, we will contact the Inter-University Consortium

question.text: for Political and Social Research (ICPSR) at the University of Michigan about archiving the data

json.answer: on a permanent basis. We do not anticipate additional costs for preparing data and

question.text: documentation for archiving. Potential secondary users of the data include institutional

json.answer: researchers, policy analysts, and higher education scholars.

question.text: We do not intend to generate metadata from this project. We do not anticipate holding

json.answer: intellectual property rights to these data.

question.text: The P.I., Professor Steven Brint, will be responsible for all data collection and precautions for

json.answer: the security and confidentiality of the data.
